headline: High: CrewAI’s default shared workspace and shell/network tools create dangerous cross-agent leakage and action-conflict pathways with the content-writing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI exposes stdin/stdout, files, and shared-memory crew behavior, so content from agent_a can be fed into agent_b and treated as instructions. agent_a is a content-writing agent with broad network egress, which can generate attacker-controlled text; agent_b can read files and run browsers/subprocesses. No direct provenance or isolation is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b prompts or files without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF agent_b parses agent_a-generated text as instructions, the attack path is active.
mitigations: Add explicit provenance labels to all agent_a outputs.
Insert a human review step before agent_b consumes agent_a text.
Restrict agent_b to read-only inputs for agent_a artifacts.
Use a delimiter/escaping convention for all copied content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while agent_a can emit arbitrary content over the network. CrewAI also touches developer-passed data and API keys. If both agents share a workspace, agent_b can read files containing agent_a outputs or secrets and transmit them onward; the profiles do not show isolation by default, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a writes sensitive outputs into the shared working directory, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b forwards workspace contents to model providers or tools, those contents can leave the host.
mitigations: Move agent outputs into separate directories.
Remove secrets from the shared workspace before agent_b runs.
Disable network egress for agent_b when processing sensitive files.
Rotate any API keys exposed to the crew.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem and network sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or emit externally: agent_a has broad network egress, and agent_b can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and use broad network egress. CrewAI’s concurrency model allows multiple instances with developer-defined shared state and no default self-isolation, so overlapping writes to the same workspace or downstream resources can race and corrupt state. The pairwise conflict is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or remote resource, write conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b instances share state without locking, concurrent updates can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent runs against the same resource.
Use append-only logs for intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, so agent_b may treat agent_a’s content as authoritative unless the orchestrator adds verification. agent_a is a content-writing agent, making it likely to produce facts or recommendations that agent_b can operationalize via shell or browser actions. That creates a direct cascade from generated text to downstream action with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without an explicit verification step, cascading error is active.
IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated facts to drive shell or browser actions, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action-taking tool call.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted drafts.
Limit agent_b to read-only analysis for agent_a content.
Add a second-pass checker for factual claims.
requires-engineering: implement policy gates before execution tools.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and has broad network egress plus filesystem access; agent_a can also emit content over the network. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the crew, CrewAI’s default lack of self-isolation can create retention and residency ambiguity. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into the crew, it may be retained or forwarded by agent_b tools.
IF agent_a or agent_b sends data to external model providers, residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Do not pass regulated data into the crew.
Redact secrets before execution.
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings.
Set explicit retention limits in the host environment.
requires-engineering: add compliance-aware routing and audit logging.
